blocking_item.summary: The UNITY_LICENSE secret holds a genuine entitlement licence (5434 bytes, root <root>, with <EntitlementGroups> and <Signature>). Run 37252858463 (2026-10-05) is the first in which the entitlement branch executed AND completed: the licence was visible in the container, the Licensing Client launched and connected, and the editor started - then rejected the licence. An entitlement licence is a NAMED-USER licence: the file carries the entitlement, but the Licensing Client needs the account's ACCESS TOKEN to resolve it, and a token exists only after a sign-in.
blocking_item.verified: Run 37252858463 job log, step 9 (91 s, conclusion success): probe printed '-rw------- 1 1001 1001 5434 Oct 5 01:48 UnityEntitlementLicense.xml' and 'Probe exit code: 0'; editor printed 'Unity Editor version: 6000.5.9f1 (b57deb96f08d)', 'Batch mode: YES', 'Successfully launched the LicensingClient (PId: 27)', 'Successfully connected to: "LicenseClient-root"', 'Version: 1.18.3+d7ffd15'; then '[Licensing::Module] Error: Access token is unavailable; failed to update', '[Licensing::Client] Error: Code 404 while processing request (status: Found 0 entitlement groups and 0 free entitlements matching requested entitlement ids)', "[Licensing::Module] Error: 'com.unity.editor.headless' was not found.", 'No valid Unity Editor license found. Please activate your license.', 'Editor exit code: 198'.
blocking_item.correction: Run 37111124148 (run 25) hung for 6h00m08s and the log could not say whether the licence was even visible in the container. Run 26 answered that: it is visible, the client launches, and the editor starts. The hang was not a visibility or network problem.
blocking_item.effect: The entitlement step now signs in before the benchmark when UNITY_EMAIL and UNITY_PASSWORD are present (-username / -password), which is what obtains the access token, and dumps the Licensing Client's own log on a non-zero exit. The preflight reports 'Unity credentials present: yes|no' so the log says up front whether the XML route can work.
blocking_item.required_secrets: UNITY_LICENSE (the entitlement XML) + UNITY_EMAIL + UNITY_PASSWORD. The XML route needs all three; the file alone is provably insufficient.
blocking_item.warning: Do not read the entitlement path as working. The sign-in fix is reasoned from the log, not tested. Two things could still fail and both are visible in the run log: the account may have two-factor authentication enabled (the CLI sign-in has no TOTP path), or the entitlement may be bound to the machine that activated it.
blocking_item.fallback: UNITY_SERIAL + UNITY_EMAIL + UNITY_PASSWORD. Re-issues the licence for the runner and needs no file. The preflight routes that combination to game-ci's activation step (the gate job runs 'Run the benchmark (serial / ULF)' and skips the entitlement step). Setup: Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions -> New repository secret, add UNITY_SERIAL (the Plus/Pro serial from Unity Hub -> Preferences -> Licenses, format XX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX), plus UNITY_EMAIL and UNITY_PASSWORD (the same account credentials the entitlement route uses). Requires a Plus/Pro seat - Unity Personal has no serial. Each activation is machine-bound and a seat allows two simultaneous activations, so a busy repo can exhaust the limit and activations then have to be released from the Unity account licence page.
blocking_item.serial_route_workflow_change: The serial route already had PRIORITY (the preflight tests UNITY_SERIAL before UNITY_LICENSE). What was missing was the WITHHOLDING. The gate step passed BOTH secrets to game-ci, and game-ci activates from the license FILE whenever one is present and only falls back to the serial when it is not - so with the entitlement XML still in UNITY_LICENSE the serial would have been silently ignored and the step would have re-run the Code 400 failure. The step now passes UNITY_LICENSE only when the preflight classified it as a ulf: `UNITY_LICENSE: ${{ needs.preflight.outputs.format == 'ulf' && secrets.UNITY_LICENSE || '' }}`. On the serial route game-ci receives exactly the documented professional environment (UNITY_SERIAL + UNITY_EMAIL + UNITY_PASSWORD), and the preflight also prints that a present UNITY_LICENSE will be withheld. Consequence: if both a valid .ulf and a serial are configured, the serial wins and the .ulf is withheld, so the run spends an activation rather than using the file.
blocking_item.serial_route_unverified: No run has ever taken the serial route. The wiring is syntactically valid (YAML parses, shell passes bash -n) and matches game-ci's documented activation, but nothing in this repository proves Unity activates with it. The first serial-route run IS the verification step.

serial_route_setup.serial_location: Unity Hub -> gear icon -> Preferences -> Licenses (the seat's serial), or the Unity account licence page at id.unity.com. Format XX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX.
serial_route_setup.github_path: Repository -> Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions -> New repository secret. Names are case-sensitive: UNITY_SERIAL, UNITY_EMAIL, UNITY_PASSWORD.
serial_route_setup.password_note: UNITY_PASSWORD is the account password, NOT a 2FA code. The CLI activation has no TOTP path, so an account with 2FA enabled can still fail.
serial_route_setup.rerun: Actions -> Water Gate -> Run workflow (branch main), or push any commit under Assets/Scripts/Water/.
serial_route_setup.confirmation: The preflight prints 'A Unity serial is present; the gate will activate with it via game-ci.' and the gate job runs 'Run the benchmark (serial / ULF)' while skipping 'Run the benchmark (entitlement XML)'.
serial_route_setup.requires: A Plus/Pro seat. Unity Personal has no serial to enter.
serial_route_setup.activation_limit: Each activation is machine-bound; a seat allows two simultaneous activations (Unity documents two per seat). A busy repo can exhaust the limit, and CI-created activations are often NOT listed on the Unity ID activation page, so the usual 'Remove selected activations' remedy may not show them - the seat can lock itself out.

conventions.assembly_rule: An assembly may only reference assemblies below it. Enforced by .asmdef references, so a violation is a compile error.
conventions.hard_prohibition: No #if UNITY_ANDROID anywhere under PET.Edit or PET.Save.
never_cut: The three shaping tools (terraforming, water, planting)
conventions.cut_order: Cuts come from the top of the written order in Deliverable 5 S08. Do not skip a row. Do not cut two things at once. A cut is recorded in the same commit that takes it.
conventions.commits: Conventional Commits; scope is the assembly without the prefix or an area (art, ci, docs, board).
conventions.branches: Trunk-based. main always compiles and passes the gate. wk/NN-slug, exp/slug, fix/slug. Never commit directly to main except docs and the board data file.
conventions.falling_behind_trigger: Two consecutive milestones missing their exit criterion. Re-read Deliverable 5 S08 before taking any cut.
